articles.title: Steven Adams Jokes Grand Theft Auto VI Will Result in Performance Declines from NBA, NFL Players
articles.summary: Houston Rockets center Steven Adams is theorizing that the upcoming release of Grand Theft Auto VI will distract players and coaches across sports this fall.
articles.body:
Houston Rockets center Steven Adams is theorizing that the upcoming release of Grand Theft Auto VI will distract players and coaches across sports this fall.

"You guys should anticipate November. The performance of the league, league-wide— GTA is dropping," Adams joked during the Rockets' Tuesday media day . "So look at NFL, look at all the leagues, and watch them plummet, mate."

"Just for the month of November, performance is gonna go down," Adams continued. "It should come back up, though. Most of the boys will get it done. Hopefully they finish the game.

"Coaching as well, by the way. The coaching and scouts are going to be horrendous, just for November, but it should bounce back in December, hopefully."

GTA VI is set to release Nov. 19, about a month after the start of the NBA regular season.

Rockstar Games celebrated the lead-up to the release by announcing last week the game will be accompanied by a 34-track album, of which six singles are currently available.

The upcoming game and album are being released simultaneously more than 13 years after GTA V dropped in September 2013.

Multiple NBA stars including Cooper Flagg and LeBron James have expressed their excitement for the next installment since GTA VI was first announced in December 2023 with an initial release target of 2025.

Adams isn't the first player to discuss the impact of the release on fall sports. New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye told WEEI earlier this month he might wait until "a break or bye week" to start playing the game.

The GTA VI release is scheduled during the Patriots' upcoming Week 11 bye , with the Atlanta Falcons, Cleveland Browns, Green Bay Packers, Los Angeles Rams and Seattle Seahawks also set to be off.

Adams is heading into his third season with the Rockets after missing a chunk of last season following season-ending ankle surgery in February.

articles.title: ¡Vuelve EuroLeague & Friends Made in Spain con Juancho Hernangomez!
articles.standfirst: El alero del Panathinaikos abre la segunda temporda del podcast en español de EuroLeague este miércoles 23 a partir de las 18.00 en MARCA.com
articles.summary: El alero del Panathinaikos abre la segunda temporda del podcast en español de EuroLeague este miércoles 23 a partir de las 18.00 en MARCA.com
articles.body: EuroLeague & Friends Made in Spain vuelve a lo grande con un invitado estelar para abrir la segunda temporada del podcast, en colaboración con MARCA. Tras una arrolladora primera temporada, el redactor de EuroLeague Javier Gancedo y el ex-jugador Quino Colom, campeón del mundo con España en 2019, vuelven para hablar de baloncesto con invitados de gran nivel y en un tono distendido. En el fondo, EuroLeague & Friends Made in Spain es una charla de amigos entre gente que sabe de lo que habla. Este primer programa de la segunda temporada se podrá ver este miércoles 23 de septiembra a partir de las 18.00 horas. La mejor previa al comienzo de la Liga regular de la Euroliga 2026-27. En esta occasion, Javi y Quino se han ido hasta el Telekom Center de Atenas, Grecia, la cancha del Panathinaikos AKTOR Athens, a hablar con Juancho Hernangomez, que ya ha empezado su cuarta temporada con el equipo. Como Quino, Juancho estaba en la selección española campeona del mundo en 2019, y también ganó el EuroBasket 2022 con España. Tras siete temporadas en la NBA y con muchas ofertas encima de la mesa, Juancho decidió fichar por Panathinaikos y poco a poco se ha convertido en una de las personas más famosas de toda Grecia, reconocido en todas partes. Su papel protagonista en una película de Netflix, Hustle, multiplicó exponencialmente su popularidad. En poco más de 40 minutos, Juancho habla con Quino y Javi de su llegada a Atenas y un divertido incidente que tuvo el primer día, lo bien que lleva la fama, la importancia de su familia y los valores que le han inculcado, su etapa en la NBA y cómo acabó teniendo a Nikola Jokic como su mejor amigo en la competición. Tambien habló con mucha naturalidad sobre su compromiso social y cómo utiliza su fama para mejorar las vidas de la gente, lo que se siente al vivir un derbi griego desde dentro y lo difícil que fue para la familia de Panathinaikos que Olympiacos ganase la EuroLeague en su propia cancha. Panathinaikos es una familia, liderada por su dueño Dimitris Giannakopoulos, que mantiene una relación excelente con Juancho hasta el punto de decir que representa los valores de su club mejor que nadie. Juancho habla de la relación con sus compañeros y sus familias, hasta el punto de que los hijos de algunos jugadores lo llaman "El Tío Juancho". Todo en un ambiente distendido, con muchas bromas y muy buen rollo. ¡No os podéis perder el nuevo episodio de EuroLeague & Friends Made in Spain!

images.caption: Juancho Hernangómez en el podcast de la Euroliga.

articles.title: El Gran Canaria estrena presidente y patrocinador
articles.standfirst: Josemi Alamo se pone al mando del Cajasiete Gran Canaria
articles.summary: Josemi Alamo se pone al mando del Cajasiete Gran Canaria
articles.body: El Cajasiete Gran Canaria ha comenzado oficialmente la temporada del 'Abonate a Volver'. Hoy se ha presentado el nuevo patrocinador del equipo, Cajasiete, y a su nuevo presidente, José Miguel Álamo: "Está todo inventado. Vengo a sumar, a arrimar el hombro, a tratar de que los jugadores estén contentos y a que la afición sea feliz", ha expresado emocionado ante la prensa. Álamo atesora una amplia trayectoria política ligada al Cabildo de Gran Canaria y a la gestión de diferentes áreas de la administración pública. Entre 2003 y 2007 ejerció como consejero de Deportes de la institución insular, mientras que posteriormente asumió responsabilidades en Educación, Universidad y Nuevas Tecnologías, Agricultura, Ganadería y Pesca y Política Social. Entre 2015 y 2019 fue concejal del Ayuntamiento de Las Palmas de Gran Canaria dentro del grupo municipal liderado por Juan José Cardona. En mayo de 2021 regresó al Cabildo como miembro del Grupo Popular y, durante el actual mandato 2023-2027, continúa como consejero de la oposición. En el ámbito universitario, actualmente ocupa el cargo de vicerrector de Cultura, Deporte y Sociedad de la Universidad de Las Palmas de Gran Canaria. Álamo asumirá la presidencia del Granca en uno de los momentos más exigentes de la historia reciente del club. Tras el descenso de categoría, el principal reto deportivo será recuperar cuanto antes la plaza en la Liga Endesa. Pero su llegada también supone el inicio de una nueva etapa institucional para una entidad de titularidad pública. La nueva dirección deberá trabajar en la consolidación de la estabilidad económica y social del club, además de afrontar el desafío deportivo con el objetivo de devolver al Gran Canaria a la máxima categoría del baloncesto español.

images.caption: La nueva familia del Cajasiete Gran Canaria Gran Canaria.

articles.title: Kevin Durant's Rockets Future Updated by GM Rafael Stone Ahead of 2026-27 NBA Season
articles.summary: Kevin Durant's future with the Houston Rockets is going to be a focal point until there's a new contract in place since he has one more season remaining before his 2027-28 player option, but general manager Rafael Stone expressed plenty of optimism ahead of the new campaign.
articles.body:
Kevin Durant's future with the Houston Rockets is going to be a focal point until there's a new contract in place since he has one more season remaining before his 2027-28 player option, but general manager Rafael Stone expressed plenty of optimism ahead of the new campaign.

Stone told Rockets insider Ben DuBose the future Hall of Famer expressed at the end of the 2025-26 season "how happy he is here" and that he wants to remain with Houston.

According to Adam Wexler of Sports Talk 790, Stone added: "His fit's been really good. It feels like he's really happy to be here, he's been a good teammate. He just wants to hoop, which fits great with our culture. We'll definitely sit down and talk at the end of this year (as he reaches the player option on his contract)."

While Durant may not be at the peak of his career at this point, his first season with the Rockets was strong.

The 37-year-old was an All-NBA Second Team selection and All-Star while averaging 26.0 points, 5.5 rebounds and 4.8 assists per game. He connected on 52 percent of his field-goal attempts and 41.3 percent of his three-pointers as well.

The efficiency stood out and was a major reason Houston reached the playoffs, although he was limited to just one postseason appearance because of injury. His team couldn't overcome his absence and lost to the Los Angeles Lakers in the first round.

With Fred VanVleet set to return to a lineup that also features Alperen Şengün, Amen Thompson and Jabari Smith Jr. around Durant, it would be anything but surprising if the Rockets were once again a factor in the Western Conference playoff race.

That is surely what the front office wants to see when it is evaluating Durant's future, although it sounds like there is mutual interest in him returning beyond just the upcoming season.

If there is, the Rockets can continue building around him as they attempt to take the next step in the West.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark's Chiefs-Inspired Nike Caitlin 1 Shoe Revealed by Andy Reid in New Video
articles.summary: Andy Reid will get the chance to be the first person other than Caitlin Clark to debut a Kansas City Chiefs-inspired colorway of the Nike Caitlin 1.
articles.body:
Andy Reid will get the chance to be the first person other than Caitlin Clark to debut a Kansas City Chiefs-inspired colorway of the Nike Caitlin 1.

The Chiefs shared a video Tuesday of Reid showing off his "Sea of Red" colorway from the Indiana Fever star's upcoming signature line.

Clark previously said in a January appearance on Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce's New Heights podcast she wanted Reid to someday coach in her signature shoes.

She then debuted her "Sea of Red" colorway ahead of the Fever's Sunday loss to the Washington Mystics.

The first retail release for some colorways of the Nike Caitlin 1 is scheduled for Oct. 1.

articles.title: Rockets' Amen Thompson Says Uber Eats Was 1st Thing He Bought After Landing $208M Contract
articles.summary: Amen Thompson didn't exactly splurge right away after signing a five-year, $208 million extension with the Houston Rockets in September.
articles.body:
Amen Thompson didn't exactly splurge right away after signing a five-year, $208 million extension with the Houston Rockets in September.

"Probably some Uber Eats," a smiling Thompson admitted after being asked what he bought first following the extension, before he recounted his order. "I get ChopShop. I try to eat kinda healthy. So I get original ChopShop and I get the fruit cup... it's so boring, don't order it."

Original ChopShop is a health-food restaurant with locations in Arizona, Texas and Georgia.

The Rockets will take boring if it means Thompson is eating healthy and taking care of his body. Houston relied heavily on the 23-year-old last season, with Thompson appearing in 79 games and averaging 37.4 minutes per game (second only to Tyrese Maxey). He also set career highs in scoring (18.3 PPG) and assists (5.3 APG) while remaining elite on the defensive end.

So nobody on the Rockets is going to be complaining about those healthy fruit bowls.

articles.title: Kawhi Leonard Joins LeBron, More In Exclusive NBA Earnings Club After New Raptors Contract
articles.summary: Kawhi Leonard is on track to join an exclusive club of players making half a billion in NBA salary after agreeing to an extension with the Toronto Raptors.
articles.body:
Kawhi Leonard is on track to join an exclusive club of players making half a billion in NBA salary after agreeing to an extension with the Toronto Raptors.

Leonard has agreed to a two-year, $115 million extension with the Raptors after his trade from the Los Angeles Clippers was finalized last week, per ESPN's Shams Charania .

The new deal is set to bring Leonard's total career earnings to $543 million, per ESPN's Bobby Marks .

NBA Europe Games Sell Out with Highest Demand Ever

LeBron James, Kevin Durant and Stephen Curry are the only players who will have received more than $500 million in NBA career earnings by the end of the 2026-27 season, per Spotrac .

Leonard and James Harden are on track to join that club in the future after signing their extensions with the Raptors and Cleveland Cavaliers, respectively.

James leads all players with $585 million in career earnings through the end of the 2026-27 season, per Spotrac . He is followed on the list by Durant ($545 million) and Curry ($532 million).

The three-year, $97 million extension Harden agreed to last month with the Cavaliers is set to bring his career earnings to a total of $511 million, per Charania .

By the time Leonard's extension wraps up at the end of the 2029-30 season, Spotrac projects three more players will have eclipsed the $500 million mark in the Phoenix Suns' Devin Booker, Boston Celtics' Paul George and Philadelphia 76ers' Joel Embiid.

On track to join the club by the end of the 2030-31 campaign is the Cavaliers' Donovan Mitchell, per Spotrac.

Leonard has received the bulk of his career earnings from the Clippers ($291.8 million) to go along with $185.4 million from the Raptors and $63.4 million from the San Antonio Spurs, per Spotrac . He was ranked by Forbes as the world's 37th highest-paid athlete of 2026.

His extension with the Raptors comes shortly after the NBA issued him a $700,000 fine as part of its investigation into alleged salary cap circumvention by the Clippers.

Leonard, who averaged 27.9 points in 65 games during a resurgent final season with the Clippers, will now head back to Toronto for the first time since leading his former team to a title in 2019.

articles.title: Buddy Hield Reportedly Traded to Hornets in 3-Player Deal, Hawks Land Dorian Finney-Smith
articles.summary: The Charlotte Hornets acquired veteran sharpshooter Buddy Hield in a trade with the Atlanta Hawks on Tuesday, according to ESPN's Shams Charania.
articles.body:
The Charlotte Hornets acquired veteran sharpshooter Buddy Hield in a trade with the Atlanta Hawks on Tuesday, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

The Hawks sent Hield, guard Ryan Nembhard and cash to the Hornets in exchange for forward Dorian Finney-Smith, per Charania.

Charlotte likely created a $4.5 million trade exception heading into the 2026-27 season due to the move, while Atlanta created a $2.1 million trade exception (h/t ESPN's Bobby Marks ).

While the trade occurred close to the beginning of preseason for both teams, it doesn't come as a complete shock.

On Sunday, NBA insider Jake Fischer reported that Atlanta and Charlotte had engaged in discussions surrounding a swap of Hield and Finney-Smith.

Hield appeared in 51 combined games with the Hawks and Golden State Warriors last year, averaging 7.6 points and 2.3 rebounds in 16.1 minutes per game while shooting 43.7 percent from the field and 34.9 percent from behind the arc.

It's worth noting that his three-point accuracy improved after he was traded to Atlanta during the season, connecting on 41.2 percent of his triples across seven games with the Hawks. Hield also shot 55.6 percent on catch-and-shoot threes during that span (via NBA.com ).

He'll carry a $9.7 million cap hit for the 2026-27 season before holding a $10.1 million player option for the following year (via Spotrac ).

Nembhard is entering his second season in the association after suiting up in 60 games with the Dallas Mavericks during his 2025-26 campaign. He was initially acquired by Atlanta in a three-team trade on July 19.

The 23-year-old showcased his playmaking abilities as a rookie, recording 6.6 points and 5.3 assists compared to just 1.4 turnovers per game. He also compiled 41.5/35.6/80.6 shooting splits.

Nembhard will earn $2.2 million next season until he hits restricted free agency in 2027.

As for Finney-Smith, he played in 37 games for the Houston Rockets last season after missing the beginning of the year while recovering from ankle surgery .

He struggled offensively after returning, shooting just 33.3 percent from the field and 27.0 percent from three-point territory.

Still, Finney-Smith has hit 35.9 percent of his threes throughout his career and brings plenty of experience to Atlanta. He has 44 playoff games under his belt.

Both the Hawks and Hornets enter the 2026-27 season looking to climb further up the Eastern Conference standings.

Atlanta is coming off a 46-36 finish to go along with a first-round playoff appearance, while Charlotte posted a 44-38 record and won a play-in tournament game.

articles.title: Scariolo pone su sello al nuevo BC Roma: ambición y Luka Doncic
articles.standfirst: El italiano, exentrenador del Madrid y de la selección española entre otros, será asesor del ambicioso proyecto romano
articles.summary: El italiano, exentrenador del Madrid y de la selección española entre otros, será asesor del ambicioso proyecto romano
articles.body: El italiano Sergio Scariolo, exentrenador de la selección española, aseguró este martes a EFE en la presentación del BC Roma, un nuevo club en la capital italiana del que forma parte como asesor, que es un proyecto "interesante" que se está construyendo "deprisa y corriendo" pero "con ideas ambiciosas". El que fuera técnico de clubes como el Real Madrid, Unicaja, el Tau Vitoria o el Virtus Bolonia, evitó hacer declaraciones sobre su reciente salida del club blanco y se centró en resaltar el proyecto del flagrante equipo romano, presentado este martes en un evento en Roma. "Aquí estamos para hablar del Roma y de este proyecto, que es un proyecto interesante, obviamente a medio-lago plazo, que se está construyendo deprisa y corriendo, pero con buenos miembros y con ideas ambiciosas", aseveró a esta agencia, al agregar que, pese a seguir viviendo en España, viaja a Roma dos días por semana y está presente todos los días de forma remota. El nuevo equipo en Roma fue presentado al público después del traslado del Vanoli Cremona a la capital italiana, y disputará su primer encuentro este sábado contra el Universo Treviso Basket. El proyecto cuenta entre sus inversores con Luka Doncic y Donnie Nelson, mientras que Scariolo, que con España fue campeón del mundo en 2019, ganó cuatro Eurobasket (2009, 2011, 2015 y 2022), logró un bronce europeo en 2017, una plata olímpica en Londres 2012 y un bronce en Río 2016, forma parte del mismo como asesor. El club presentó el 14 de septiembre su escudo y su identidad visual, inspirados en la historia y la arquitectura de Roma. En el centro del emblema aparece la diosa Roma, tomada de representaciones de antiguas monedas romanas. El nacimiento del BC Roma se produce seis años después de la salida de la histórica Virtus Roma de la Serie A por problemas económicos. La ciudad del centro de Italia recupera así presencia en la máxima categoría, en una nueva etapa en la que también participa el Maxima Roma, otro club creado en 2026.

images.caption: Sergio Scariolo y Luka Doncic impulsarán el proyecto del nuevo BC Roma. EFE/ LAPRESSE

articles.title: Tyrese Maxey Likens LeBron James to a 'Big Brother,' Talks Process of Star Signing 76ers Contract
articles.summary: In August, Philadelphia 76ers guard VJ Edgecombe suggested that Tyrese Maxey knew all along that the team was going to land LeBron James.
articles.body:
In August, Philadelphia 76ers guard VJ Edgecombe suggested that Tyrese Maxey knew all along that the team was going to land LeBron James.

While Maxey denied those claims, he did say on Tuesday that he views James as a friend and a brotherly figure.

"I'm not going to say I knew and just didn't tell anyone, but I had multiple conversations with LeBron," he told Tomer Azarly of ClutchPoints. "I work out with LeBron early in the morning, and that's just off of being cool with him. It's funny, he's like a big brother, like an OG to me, and for us to be teammates, it was funny because a kid asked me the other day, he looked at me and said, 'Are you and LeBron friends?' I thought about it. I leaned back and I said, 'You know, I guess we are friends. He's the old, old, old guy, but he's like one of my old friends.' It's funny because we are teammates now, co-workers, but it's kind of like a big brother situation. It's going to be very cool and interesting dynamic."

The Sixers had quite the offseason, adding James and Jaylen Brown to the core of Maxey, Edgecombe and Joel Embiid while bolstering the bench with the signings of Dean Wade, Anfernee Simons and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope and the first-round selection of Labaron Philon Jr.

Excitement abounds in Philly, though there are questions about how the team's cast of stars will coexist.

"We haven't gotten on the court yet, so we'll see," Maxey told Azarly. "But as far as the chemistry off the court, guys are communicating, guys are having a good time doing it, guys are really pumping each other up, and guys are also willing to sacrifice. It's just what they've said. So when we step on the court, we have to kind of embody all those things that we've been talking about. Sacrificing, coming together as one, and going out there competing every single night. Those are the three things that we really have to focus on. It's going to be one day at a time. One day at a time and one step at a time. There's going to be some good days, there's going to be some bad days, but at the end of the day we always want to be stepping in the right direction to come playoff time."

The expectation is that James will act as the team's de facto point guard, which in turn will allow Maxey to operate off the ball more (a role he thrived in while playing next to James Harden). How the shots will be distributed with four heavy-usage players in the starting lineup (plus a burgeoning young star in Edgecombe who also needs touches) remains to be seen.

But the talent is unmistakable and excitement levels are high ahead of the team's Media Day on Monday.

articles.title: El último baile de Kawhi será en Toronto: 115 millones de dólares
articles.standfirst: El alero de 35 años amplía su contrato con los Raptors por dos temporadas hasta la 2028-29
articles.summary: El alero de 35 años amplía su contrato con los Raptors por dos temporadas hasta la 2028-29
articles.body: Kawhi Leonard seguirá en los Toronto Raptors. La estrella de la franquicia canadiense ha alcanzado un acuerdo para ampliar su contrato por dos temporadas y 115 millones de dólares, con una opción de jugador para la campaña 2028-29. El alero, de 35 años, quiere poner punto final a su carrera en Toronto, donde ya fue campeón de la NBA en 2019. El acuerdo lo adelanta ESPN, que cita a su agente, Harrison Gaines, de Slash Sports. Leonard ha aceptado cobrar 11 millones de dólares menos que el máximo al que podía aspirar con su extensión y también ha renunciado a una bonificación de 7,45 millones de dólares vinculada a su traspaso desde los Clippers. Un gesto que permite a los Raptors ganar margen de maniobra en un escenario marcado por el crecimiento de su presupuesto salarial. Con el nuevo acuerdo, Leonard queda ligado a Toronto por un contrato de tres años y 165 millones de dólares. La renovación llega después de un verano convulso alrededor del jugador. Toronto y los Clippers habían acordado el 30 de junio su traspaso, pero la operación quedó temporalmente bloqueada por la investigación de la NBA sobre las posibles irregularidades de Los Ángeles en relación con el límite salarial. Finalmente, la Liga sancionó a los Clippers con la pérdida de cinco primeras rondas, una multa de 30 millones de dólares y una suspensión de un año para su propietario, Steve Ballmer. Leonard, por su parte, pagó 700.000 dólares en concepto de restitución por beneficios indebidos relacionados con su tío y antiguo representante, Dennis Robertson. Ahora, Leonard afronta una nueva etapa en Toronto, donde ya dejó una huella imborrable al conquistar el primer anillo de la historia de los Raptors y ser elegido MVP de aquellas Finales de 2019. Viene, además, de firmar la temporada más anotadora de su carrera, con 27,9 puntos de media en 65 partidos con los Clippers. Siete veces All-Star, siete veces incluido en el mejor quinteto de la NBA y dos veces campeón, el alero vuelve a comprometer su futuro con una franquicia en la que busca cerrar el círculo de su carrera.

articles.title: Los Hawks sacuden el mercado NBA: Entregan a Hield y Nembhard a cambio de Finney-Smith
articles.standfirst: Atlanta se refuerza con músculo y experiencia con el veterano alero de los Hornets
articles.summary: Atlanta se refuerza con músculo y experiencia con el veterano alero de los Hornets
articles.body: Los Atlanta Hawks mueven ficha y refuerzan su plantilla con un jugador de experiencia y recorrido en la NBA. La franquicia de Georgia traspasará a Buddy Hield, Ryan Nembhard y una cantidad de dinero a los Charlotte Hornets a cambio de Dorian Finney-Smith, según adelantó Shams Charania, de ESPN. Hield llegó a Atlanta el pasado verano dentro de la operación que llevó a Kristaps Porzingis a los Golden State Warriors. Sin embargo, el escolta apenas disputó siete partidos con los Hawks la pasada temporada. Ahora tiene por delante un contrato de 9,5 millones de dólares para esta campaña y una opción de jugador de algo más de 10 millones para la 2027-28. Finney-Smith, por su parte, aterrizó en Charlotte procedente de los Houston Rockets al inicio de la pretemporada. El veterano alero tiene todavía tres años de contrato y 53 millones de dólares por cobrar, con una opción de jugador para la temporada 2028-29. En la operación también entra Ryan Nembhard, base de 23 años que no fue elegido en el Draft y llegó a Atlanta en el traspaso a tres bandas que implicó a Zaccharie Risacher y Luguentz Dort. La pasada temporada promedió 6,6 puntos y 5,3 asistencias en 19,5 minutos por partido.

articles.title: Deion Sanders dismisses multiple players after locker room incident following Colorado's loss to Northwestern
articles.summary: Safety Ben Finneseth publicly apologized for pregame trash talk as Deion Sanders vowed to crack down on conduct detrimental to Colorado football.
articles.body: Deion Sanders has obviously not been in the best of moods following Colorado's 41-7 loss to Northwestern this past weekend, and he showed just how upset he was this week with players on his team. Before Colorado took the field against the Wildcats, multiple players were captured on video talking trash about the size of Northwestern’s crowd. It turned out to be the beginning of an unpleasant day for everyone involved with the Buffaloes. Not only did the Buffaloes get torched on the field, but there were multiple players who decided that it would be in their best interest to laugh about the loss while entering the postgame locker room. FOUR DAYS IN OXFORD: INSIDE THE CHAOTIC RETURN OF LANE KIFFIN TO OLE MISS, THAT TURNED INTO PURE CINEMA "I don't understand how in the world you can find joy, or you can find a laughing matter when I'm right behind you walking [the locker room]," Sanders said after the loss. "I don't understand that, and I addressed it, and I'm going to put my foot in it, not on it." Deion Sanders trying to prevent further damage for Buffaloes Even though Colorado is 2-1 on the season, what we witnessed on Saturday could turn into a trend for a football team that looked overwhelmed for nearly the entire game against Northwestern. The last thing Deion Sanders wants is for this to snowball into another horrid season, with a select few players not taking things seriously in the locker room. So, he decided it was best for the football team to move on from a number of players, who have not been identified as of yet. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! There is also the hangover effect with this bunch from Colorado, seeing how last season turned into a nightmare for the coaching staff in Boulder. In past years, Deion might have been able to look the other way, but not any longer. The Colorado head coach made it a point to say that it was not just an incident that took place following the Northwestern game, but more so that he felt as though it was not in the best interest of his team to keep a few guys around for the sake of it. "It's never one," Sanders said on Tuesday. "I'm one the most loving and giving and forgiving men you could ever meet, but when you start [having] conduct detrimental to the team, you don't care about the team, you care about you, I have a problem with that. A year ago, I didn't put my foot down in it enough. It lingered a little bit. Then, it imploded. "I'm not doing that anymore." One player apologizes for comments made before Northwestern game To show that he wasn’t playing around when it came to his team disrespecting others, Sanders had safety Ben Finneseth appear before the head coach took to the podium in order to apologize for their pregame comments that were captured on social media. "It was childish. It was a stupid thing that I said. It won't happen again," Ben Finneseth said on Tuesday. "The way I handled it was horrible and I promise you guys that it will not happen again." Colorado will face Baylor this weekend in Waco, with plenty on the line if Deion Sanders hopes to keep his team in the running for a potential shot at a Big 12 title game appearance. articles.title: Knicks’ path to a repeat runs straight through Cleveland
articles.summary: The Knicks will not get to ease into the part of the schedule that matters. The NBA has them visiting […]
articles.body:
The Knicks will not get to ease into the part of the schedule that matters. The NBA has them visiting Cleveland on Nov. 7 at 8 p.m. ET, a national-TV rematch of last season's Eastern Conference Finals.

For the Knicks , it is more than a tidy early-season game. Cleveland was the team standing in the way before New York finished its title run, and the Cavaliers will have that date circled before the arena doors open.

The game will be on NBA TV, but it is going to feel much bigger than a normal November slot. A defending champion walking into an old playoff building is the kind of test that gets everybody's attention.

The Knicks get an early answer on the road

No regular-season game decides a repeat bid. Nobody needs to pretend Nov. 7 will settle anything. The Knicks have months of basketball ahead of them.

It will show how ready they are to handle the target on their back. Last season, every opponent wanted to knock off New York once the playoffs started. The schedule will keep offering the same chance this year.

Jalen Brunson will be the center of the attention, as usual. He has already lived through the postseason pressure that comes with being the leader of a title team. Cleveland will not make the road game easier because the calendar says November.

Cleveland has a reason to remember the Knicks

The Cavaliers are a different kind of early opponent. There is recent history attached to this one, which makes the matchup feel different before anyone jumps for the opening tip.

New York should welcome that. A champion does not get a quiet title defense, and there is no benefit in ducking the teams that have the most reason to come after them. The first trip to Cleveland will tell us plenty about the mood around this group, even if it does not settle the bigger picture.
